Text: Fewer enemies, the Guards are automatically restored to 4 after each level. Laws used in Beginner are not recorded in the Book of Laws, and achievements cannot be unlocked.
Same enemy count and behavior as Normal, but the game starts with only one Guard and recovery Laws are not offered.
Grandmaster difficulty is unlocked only after\nsuccessfully completing Campaign Mode on Normal difficulty.
The following law is in effect for this level:
No special rules. Guards normally move one square in any direction.
Guards can move only vertically or horizontally.
Guards can move only forward, forward-left, or forward-right.
Guards cannot move straight forward or backward; the other 6 directions are allowed.
Once per level, each Guard can move 2 squares horizontally or vertically if both the middle and destination squares are empty.
Once per level, each Guard can move 2 squares diagonally if both the middle and destination squares are empty.
Each Guard's first move can be 2 squares in any direction if the middle square is empty.
Each guard must alternate between orthogonal and diagonal movement.
A guard cannot repeat the same direction as its previous move.
One of the 8 directions is chosen at random and remains forbidden for the entire level.
Once per level, one Guard can move 2 squares in any direction if the middle square is empty.
After a diagonal move, that guard cannot be selected on the next turn.
Each guard's first orthogonal move causes no enemy response.
Guards cannot end their move on a road-edge square.
Once per level, each Guard can jump over one adjacent piece, friendly or enemy, and land on the empty square immediately beyond it.
When a Guard reaches the checkpoint, the enemy response is skipped and, if the level continues, the next 5 Guard moves also cause no enemy response.
Enemy Knights cannot end their move on a white square.
You cannot select the same guard on two consecutive turns.
Every active guard must move once before any of them can move again.
Each turn, the game randomly indicates which guard must move, provided it has a legal move.
Once per level, you can make one move with no enemy response, giving you 2 consecutive moves.
Every fifth guard move skips the enemy response.
Every fifth guard move grants the enemy two consecutive moves.
Enemies skip the first 3 enemy responses of the level.
After a capture, the same guard may immediately move a second time, once per turn.
If only one active guard remains, it gets two moves before each enemy response.
While all 4 guards are alive, enemies move only after every 2 player moves.
Every four guard moves, enemies can make two consecutive moves.
Once per level, you can skip one entire enemy response.
The first enemy attack that would eliminate a Guard is cancelled.
A guard cannot end more than 3 squares away from the nearest guard.
Two guards cannot end their moves on adjacent squares.
Two guards cannot occupy the same column.
Every third Guard move must be made by one of the most advanced Guards.
One random guard is marked and must remain within 1 square of the road's center line.
One random guard must make at least one capture before it can cross the checkpoint.
Two random guards must remain within 2 squares of each other.
After a Guard is lost, the next move can be 2 squares in any direction if the middle square is empty.
A marked guard cannot be captured while adjacent to another active guard.
Enemy Knights remain still and cannot capture.
Knights prefer the legal move that brings them closer to the nearest guard.
A special square appears for each missing Guard. Enter one to revive a Guard, which returns on the starting row.
Bishops choose a legal move at random within their range.
Mobile enemy pieces may choose only moves that bring them closer to the bottom edge of the screen.
Mobile enemy pieces may choose only moves that take them farther from the bottom edge.
Enemies must remain in the left or right half of the grid where they started the level.
Enemy Rooks move and capture only diagonally, like Bishops.
Only one randomly selected enemy type among those present can move or capture; all others remain still.
The same enemy cannot act in 2 consecutive enemy responses if another enemy has a legal move.
Enemy Knights can use only the L-shaped jump of 2 columns and 1 row.
If a Rook can capture, the opponent must choose a Rook capture.
Rooks, Bishops, and Queens cannot capture a Guard from 1 square away.
Rooks, Bishops, and Queens can capture a Guard only from 1 square away.
Distant enemies appear as "?" or "!" until they are within 6 rows of a Guard.
After an attack, that enemy cannot attack on the next enemy response.
The range of Rooks, Bishops, and Queens is reduced by 5 squares.
Every 15 guard moves, a random enemy Pawn transforms into a Knight.
Reduces the number of enemies in the level by 25%.
Increases the number of enemies in the level by 25%.
No enemy can be generated in the first 4 walkable rows.
At least one enemy is generated in the 3 rows before the checkpoint.
Enemies are generated preferentially on road-edge squares.
No enemy can be generated adjacent to another enemy.
Enemies prefer to appear within 2 squares of another enemy.
The first time a guard reaches halfway up the route, an enemy Pawn appears on a valid empty square.
Enemies placed in the upper half of the road are all Pawns.
The road is 2 columns wider than normal.
The road is 2 columns narrower than normal, but never below the minimum playable width.
Bends are much rarer: their probability drops to 20% of normal.
Increases the probability of changing direction by 50%.
The road tends to alternate left and right bends.
Generates 2 bottlenecks, each one row long.
During generation, the road shifts sideways by one column at regular intervals.
Forces one large S-shaped bend in the level.
The Horse in the Gray Flannel Suit
The first guard you move becomes a Knight for the rest of the level.
Guards can enter the checkpoint only with a diagonal move.
Magenta and cyan squares with the same number form a portal pair. When a Guard enters one, it teleports to the other, but only if the exit square is empty.
The active checkpoint square shifts by one column after every 2 Guard moves.
In this level, the Guards move like knights.
15 random magenta safe squares protect any guards occupying them from captures.
Generates 10 impassable magenta squares on the road.
There are 15 blocks at the start; one is removed after every 4 Guard moves.
Marked tiles can only be crossed by Guards using diagonal moves.
Whenever an enemy Knight leaves a square, that square becomes permanently impassable.
Checkpoint squares alternate between active and inactive after every Guard move.
At the start of each player turn, the enemy closest to a Guard is indicated. It will act on the next enemy response if it has a legal move.
Distant enemies appear as "?" until they are within 4 rows of a Guard.

At the start of the level, a random square shows a countdown from 5. It decreases after every Guard move. At zero, the square explodes, removes any piece on it, becomes unusable, and a new countdown square appears.
Enemy Pawns cannot capture a Guard standing on a black square.
Rooks and Bishops can move only up to a maximum distance of 5 squares.
Rooks and Bishops can move only up to a maximum distance of 2 squares.
Rooks and Bishops can move only up to a maximum distance of 1 square.
The first capture made by a Guard in the level causes no enemy response.
Every capture made by a Guard triggers one extra enemy response.
A guard that captures cannot capture again for its next 2 moves.
After a capture, if another capture is available from the new square, the same Guard may make it immediately, once.
During odd-numbered Guard moves, all enemies become invisible, but they can still capture and be captured.
One random enemy cannot be captured.
Each Guard's first capture causes no enemy response; from the second onward, every capture triggers one extra enemy response.
Every fourth team move may cover two orthogonal squares along a clear path.
Every fifth team move must be diagonal.
Immediately after the player's 10th move, Rooks, Bishops, and Queens get one extra enemy move.
Enemies are concentrated in two separate bands.
In this level, Guards and Enemies transform into whatever they have just captured.
When a Guard reaches the checkpoint, the enemy response to that move is skipped if the level continues.
The final third of the road is 1 column narrower.
The road is 1 column narrower, but the first enemy attack that would eliminate a Guard is cancelled.
The road has more bends, but enemies respond only after every 2 Guard moves.
Each Guard can use one 2-square Dash in any direction if the middle square is empty. Also, the same Guard cannot be selected twice in a row.
Generates 10 blocked squares and 10 magenta safe squares. A Guard on a safe square cannot be captured.
Enemies chase the nearest guard, but move only on alternating turns.
At the end of every full turn, the Royal Guard and the enemy Queen each transform independently into a random chess piece.

Disaster has struck the White Kingdom.\nThe White King is gone, kidnapped\nby the forces of the Black Queen.
As fear spreads through the empty throne room,\nfour humble pawns, the King's most loyal guards,\nswear they will bring their ruler home.
Across a land of black-and-white squares\nand ever-changing rules, four loyal pawns\nbegin their quest.
Beyond the horizon lies the Black Queen's castle.\nTheir journey begins now!
